name: sliced-text
summary: A headline cut into four vertical windows onto four copies of itself, sliding out of alignment and back into register as the section scrolls.

cells.description: How many vertical bands the word is cut into. Upstream's totalCells for effect 1.

offset.description: Percent each band starts away from register, multiplied by its distance from the centre. Upstream's fx1 initialValues.x.

deviations.what: The scroll driver is anime.js' onScroll with enter 'bottom top' and leave '10% top', not ScrollTrigger's start 'top bottom' / end 'top top+=10%' with Lenis smoothing underneath.
deviations.why: GSAP is not a dependency this library can take. The two thresholds are the same window written the other way round: anime puts the container position first and the target position second, where ScrollTrigger puts the trigger first. Lenis is dropped because smooth scrolling is a page-level choice, and paw-fx already ships smooth-scroll as its own effect for a site that wants it.

deviations.what: GSAP's power1 ease is written as anime's outQuad, which is the same quadratic curve out.
deviations.why: GSAP names its power curves by exponent minus one and defaults them to .out; anime names them after the polynomial. Same function, different spelling.

deviations.what: Only effect 1 is ported. fx2 through fx6, defaultTimeline, the data-effect switch and the fxImagesTimeline that rotates the demo's background photographs are dropped.
deviations.why: fx1 is the plainest of the six and the only one that needs nothing but the bands themselves; the others add a second axis, a rotation or a scale on top. Shipping six variants behind an option would be five untested code paths in a library where each effect is meant to be one thing. The image timeline goes because the pictures it rotates are not ours to redistribute.

deviations.what: Custom properties are renamed --fx-text-width, --fx-splits and --fx-offset from upstream's --text-width, --gsplits and --offset, and the class names are ours.
deviations.why: The effect contract prefixes every custom property --fx-, and an effect is one section among several: resolving the headings inside the mounted section is what keeps a second instance on the page independent.

deviations.what: Each heading's original innerHTML is kept and restored on destroy, along with the two custom properties, and the resize listener is removed.
deviations.why: Upstream is a demo page that never tears the effect down and leaves its resize handler bound for the life of the tab. Here a destroy would otherwise leave four column copies in the markup and a listener re-measuring detached nodes.

deviations.what: Under prefers-reduced-motion the heading is never rebuilt and no scroll observer is created.
deviations.why: Effect contract: mount() stays at rest, and the heading in the markup is already the finished content.
